questions.question: Article 21 is related to which of the following fundamental rights?

options.text: Protection of Language, Culture of Minorities
Protection of Life and Personal Liberty

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Protection of Life and Personal Liberty**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 21** of the Indian Constitution is related to the **Protection of Life and Personal Liberty**.
 
• It states that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• This article is a cornerstone of the fundamental rights provided to Indian citizens and is a crucial aspect of the right to life and personal freedom.
 
• The scope of Article 21 has been expanded through various judicial interpretations to include the right to live with human dignity, the right to livelihood, the right to health, and the right to privacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India**, adopted on 26th November 1949 and effective from 26th January 1950, provides a comprehensive framework for the political and legal system of the country.
 
• Article 21 has been instrumental in the development of various rights through judicial activism, significantly impacting the protection and enforcement of human rights in India.
 
• The interpretation of Article 21 has evolved over time, ensuring that it remains relevant to contemporary issues and challenges.
 
• Other fundamental rights, such as the right to equality (Article 14) and the right to freedom (Articles 19-22), complement the protections offered under Article 21.
 
• The judiciary plays a pivotal role in upholding and expanding the scope of Article 21 through landmark judgments and decisions.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India consists of ________ judges and Chief Judges of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__33__. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India originally started with a **Chief Justice of India** and** 7 judges in 1950,** making a** total of 8 judges.** 
 
• 1978: Increased to **18 judges**.
 
• 2009: Further expanded to** 31 judges**.
 
• 2019: Reached the current strength of** 34 judges** (**1 Chief __Justice + 33 judges).**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Recommendation by the Collegium:** The Collegium, consisting of the Chief Justice of India __(CJI) and the four senior-most judges__,__ recommends names for appointment.
 
• For the **Chief Justice**, the senior-most judge is considered.
 
 
• **Presidential Appointment:** The President of India appoints the judges based on the Collegium's recommendation and the input from the Law Ministry.
 
• This process is guided by Articles** 124 and 217** of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• The current Chief Justice of India is** **Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai (B. R. Gavai) was appointed as the 52nd Chief Justice of India on 14th May 2025 and is due to retire on 23rd November 2025, upon attaining the age of 65 years.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts of British India did the British government take direct control of the administration of India in its own hands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act 1858**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Government of India Act 1858** was the legislation that marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and transferred the control of India to the British Crown.
 
• This act was enacted in response to the Indian Rebellion of 1857, which exposed the vulnerabilities and inadequacies of the Company's administration.
 
• Under this Act, the British government established the office of the Secretary of State for India, who was given complete authority and control over the Indian administration.
 
• The Act also led to the creation of the India Council to assist the Secretary of State for India.
 
• This transition marked the beginning of the period known as the British Raj, which lasted until India's independence in 1947.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Prior to the Government of India Act 1858, the East India Company had been the ruling entity in India, having gained significant control after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.
 
• The Act was also known as the Act for the Better Government of India and was passed on August 2, 1858.
 
• It led to the establishment of the office of Viceroy of India, a position held by the Governor-General of India, who acted as the representative of the British Crown.
 
• The Act aimed to improve the governance of India by ensuring a more direct and accountable administration under the British Parliament.
 
• The administrative structure set up by this Act remained largely unchanged until the passage of the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy and federal structure.

questions.question: When was the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (**PMEGP**) was launched in the year **2008**.
 
• **PMEGP** is a credit-linked subsidy program aimed at generating self-employment opportunities through the establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector by helping traditional artisans and unemployed youth.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** at the national level and by the State KVIC Directorates, State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs), and District Industries Centers (DICs) at the state level.
 
• Under the scheme, the government provides a subsidy to the beneficiaries to set up new micro-enterprises, thereby creating employment opportunities in rural as well as urban areas.
 
• The scheme also aims to foster economic development in rural areas and to reduce regional imbalances by promoting the growth of village industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, and it functions under the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises.
 
• The scheme was formulated by merging two schemes, namely the **Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana (PMRY)** and the **Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP)**, to enhance the effectiveness of employment generation in rural and urban areas.
 
• Beneficiaries under the scheme can avail of financial assistance in the form of margin money subsidy, which is adjusted against the loan amount provided by the banks.
 
• The scheme has specific eligibility criteria, including age, educational qualification, and project cost limits, to ensure that genuine and deserving candidates benefit from it.

questions.solution:

• The **remaining 3% of Earth's water is found in glaciers, ice caps, groundwater, lakes, rivers, and the atmosphere**.
 
• Freshwater, which is essential for human consumption and agriculture, **constitutes only about 2.5-2.75% of the total water** on Earth.

• Climate change and global warming are impacting the distribution and availability of freshwater resources.
 
• Technological advances and policies aimed at **water conservation, pollution control, and efficient usage **are essential to address water scarcity issues.

questions.question: Identify an organelle found both in eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the only organelles found in both eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells.
 
• They are responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely within the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum in eukaryotic cells.
 
• In prokaryotic cells, ribosomes are smaller (70S) compared to those in eukaryotic cells (80S).
 
• Despite the size difference, the fundamental function of ribosomes remains the same across both cell types.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prokaryotic cells** do not have membrane-bound organelles, which distinguishes them from eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Eukaryotic cells** contain various membrane-bound organelles, including the nucleus, mitochondria, and lysosomes, which are absent in prokaryotic cells.
 
• The presence of ribosomes in both cell types highlights their essential role in the fundamental process of protein synthesis.
 
• The differences in ribosome size between prokaryotes and eukaryotes are due to variations in their ribosomal RNA and protein content.

questions.question: The tendency of an atom or a functional group to attract a shared pair of electrons toward itself, is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**electronegativity**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electronegativity** is the tendency of an atom or a functional group to attract a shared pair of electrons toward itself.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in chemistry that helps in understanding the behavior of atoms in molecules.
 
• Elements with high electronegativity, such as fluorine, oxygen, and nitrogen, strongly attract electrons towards themselves.
 
• The concept of electronegativity is crucial in predicting the nature of bonds between atoms, whether they will be ionic, polar covalent, or nonpolar covalent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of electronegativity was first introduced by **Linus Pauling** in 1932.
 
• Electronegativity values are often measured on the **Pauling scale**, where fluorine is assigned the highest value of 4.0.
 
• Electronegativity can influence various chemical properties, including bond strength, bond length, and the overall polarity of molecules.
 
• Understanding electronegativity is essential for predicting the behavior of molecules in chemical reactions and for designing new chemical compounds.

• This writ ensures that no person is detained unlawfully and mandates that the detained individual be brought before a court.
 
• The purpose of the writ is to provide a prompt judicial inquiry into the reasons for the detention of an individual.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The writ of **Habeas Corpus** is one of the five writs that can be issued by the courts in India under Article 32 and Article 226 of the Constitution.
 
• The other four writs include **Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo-Warranto, and Certiorari**.
 
• The term **Habeas Corpus** is derived from Latin, meaning "You shall have the body."
 
• This writ is a crucial tool for safeguarding individual freedom against arbitrary state action.
 
• The judiciary plays a vital role in upholding the rights of individuals through the issuance of the writ of **Habeas Corpus**.

questions.question: Assume that the value of the cash reserve ratio is 25%. What will be the value of money multiplier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of the **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is **25%**.
 
• The **money multiplier** is calculated as the reciprocal of the cash reserve ratio.
 
• Formula: **Money Multiplier = 1 / CRR**
 
• Given that CRR is 25%, the money multiplier is calculated as follows:
 
• **Money Multiplier = 1 / 0.25 = 4**
 
• Therefore, the value of the money multiplier is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is a percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank as reserves.
 
• The **money multiplier** effect describes how an initial deposit can lead to a larger final increase in the total money supply.
 
• A higher CRR means a lower money multiplier and vice versa.
 
• The central bank uses CRR as a tool to control liquidity in the banking system.

questions.question: Who among the following belongs to Patiala Gharana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ali Baksh Khan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ali Baksh Khan** is associated with the Patiala Gharana.
 
• The Patiala Gharana is one of the prominent gharanas (musical lineage) in Indian classical music, particularly known for its unique style and contribution to vocal music.
 
• It was founded by Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• Patiala Gharana is known for its intricate and elaborate compositions, and for incorporating elements from various other gharanas and musical traditions.
 
• Some of the notable exponents of Patiala Gharana include Bade Ghulam Ali Khan and his descendants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Patiala Gharana** is renowned for its emphasis on the use of intricate and swift taans (rapid melodic sequences) and bol-baant (rhythmic variations).
 
• Ali Baksh Khan and Fateh Ali Khan were court musicians in the royal court of Patiala, which significantly influenced the development and propagation of this gharana.
 
• The gharana has made significant contributions to the repertoire of khayal (a form of Hindustani classical music) and thumri (a semi-classical form).
 
• Patiala Gharana's singing style is marked by the use of intricate ornamentation and improvisation, which adds a unique flavor to their performances.
 
• The gharana has also produced many renowned instrumentalists, although it is primarily known for its vocal tradition.
